findings.title: x64dbg-MCP Server exposes debugger operations to unauthenticated network clients
visible_dates: NVD publication timestamp observed in keyword search: 2026-10-09T18:17:04.350
findings.affected_boundary_or_version: duty1g x64dbg-mcp-server before 1.1; default HTTP/SSE listener on 0.0.0.0, ports 9094 for x64 and 9095 for x32.
findings.summary: The CVE record says x64dbg-MCP Server exposed all MCP debugger tools over HTTP/SSE without authentication by default. Any unauthenticated network client that could reach the default port could run arbitrary x64dbg commands, attach to processes, read and write debuggee memory, and write files to arbitrary paths. Version 1.1 is listed as fixed.
findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_security: MCP servers can bridge agent tool calls into high-authority local tools. A debugger MCP server without authentication turns tool discovery into process control, memory access, and arbitrary file writes, so agent/tool deployments need network binding, authentication, and least-privilege gates.

upstream_routing.upstream_owned: ai-wiki owns broad MCP server catalog context and x64dbg-MCP Server as an ecosystem entity if durable coverage is needed.
upstream_routing.local_security_lens: Keep local coverage focused on unauthenticated MCP debugger authority, network exposure defaults, memory/process/file impact, and the 1.1 mitigation boundary.

findings.confidence_notes: High confidence from CVE Services and NVD timing. GitHub advisory pages were listed as CNA references but should be refetched during ingest for exact GHSA severity and remediation wording.

findings.title: AstronRPA smart-component chat can turn prompt-injected LLM output into desktop command execution
visible_dates: NVD publication timestamp observed in keyword search: 2026-10-09T17:16:47.027
findings.affected_boundary_or_version: iflytek AstronRPA through 1.1.6; desktop smart-component chat rendering, v-html output, unrestricted open-path IPC handler, and command execution as the desktop user.
findings.summary: The CVE record describes a desktop-client XSS in AstronRPA's smart-component chat. Attackers can place prompt-injection content in a web page so the model emits HTML event handlers; the rendered output can invoke an unrestricted IPC handler with shell metacharacters and execute commands as the desktop user.
findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_security: This is a concrete prompt-injection-to-local-action chain across web content, LLM output rendering, and a desktop IPC bridge. It illustrates why agentic desktop tools need output sanitization, explicit command mediation, and strict separation between model text and privileged local actions.

upstream_routing.upstream_owned: ai-wiki owns broad AstronRPA product/entity context if durable coverage is created.
upstream_routing.local_security_lens: Keep local coverage focused on prompt-injection, unsafe HTML rendering, IPC command mediation, and desktop agent authority.

findings.confidence_notes: High confidence for the CVE fact and timing from CVE Services/NVD. The GitHub issue and code reference are public CNA references; ingest should verify current maintainer remediation status.
follow_up_actions: During ingest, inspect the linked GitHub issue for patch or maintainer response.
Consider a model-and-prompt-security leaf because the exploit path depends on prompt-injected model output crossing into privileged UI/IPC.

findings.title: Ollama model pull path traversal can write malicious binaries outside the model store
visible_dates: NVD publication timestamp observed in keyword search: 2026-10-08T14:16:46.187
findings.affected_boundary_or_version: Ollama 0.34.2 and versions before 0.35.0 are listed as affected; unauthenticated /api/pull path traversal through insufficient digest validation.
findings.summary: The CVE record says Ollama's /api/pull endpoint insufficiently validated layer digests. An unauthenticated remote attacker could supply traversal sequences as a layer digest, write a malicious binary outside the model store, and, when the server process could write to /usr/lib/ollama as in many default Docker images, achieve code execution as root on the next server restart.
findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_security: Model acquisition endpoints are part of the AI runtime supply chain. A model-pull path traversal changes a registry/download boundary into host file write and possible root execution, so deployments need digest canonicalization, file-store confinement, and container write-permission review.

upstream_routing.upstream_owned: ai-wiki owns broad Ollama runtime and model-serving entity coverage.
upstream_routing.local_security_lens: Keep local coverage focused on model-pull path traversal, registry trust, file-store confinement, container write permissions, and fixed-version gates.

findings.confidence_notes: High confidence from CVE Services and NVD. The CERT Polska primary post is listed as the technical reference; ingest should fetch it for exact exploit preconditions and whether 0.35.0 is the first fixed release.

findings.title: SumatraPDF AI selection-translate command builder can inject agentic CLI arguments
visible_dates: NVD publication timestamp observed in keyword search: 2026-10-08T23:17:00.320
findings.affected_boundary_or_version: SumatraPDF 3.6.1 and earlier; Windows AI selection-translate paths BuildGrokTranslateCmdLineTemp(), BuildClaudeTranslateCmdLineTemp(), and BuildCodexTranslateCmdLineTemp(); no fixed version was listed in the CVE text.
findings.summary: The CVE record says selected or pasted translation text is embedded in quoted Windows command lines with incomplete escaping. When a corresponding agentic CLI backend is installed and used, attacker-controlled document text can inject model, working-directory, approval, or sandbox-bypass flags.
findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_security: Document-to-agent translation bridges untrusted document text into AI CLI invocation. Argument injection can alter model/tool execution policy and local sandbox boundaries, so desktop AI integrations need structured process invocation and strict argument separation.

upstream_routing.upstream_owned: ai-wiki owns broad product or agentic CLI entity context for Grok, Claude, Codex, and SumatraPDF if needed.
upstream_routing.local_security_lens: Keep local coverage focused on untrusted document text crossing into agentic CLI arguments, approval/sandbox flag injection, and desktop workflow controls.

findings.confidence_notes: High confidence for CVE timing and affected functions from CVE Services/NVD. Ingest should inspect the GitHub advisory and commit to confirm whether the patch fully replaces quoted string assembly with structured argument handling.
follow_up_actions: During ingest, verify the GitHub advisory for affected versions and remediation state.
Classify under agent/tool security or model/prompt security depending on the final leaf boundary.
